manual.text:
## Specific task description

Task instruction: Pick up the green orange and place it in the bowl.

Task description: Use the right gripper to place the green orange on the table into the light blue bowl.

Success criteria: The green orange rests securely inside and is supported by the bowl; the gripper is open and the fruit released.

## Execution tips

- Let the pads grip opposite sides around the widest middle section of the orange, with an opening slightly wider than that section. Avoid grasping only the sloped top, which could let it slip out.
- Before closing, use both views to confirm that the fingers are on opposite sides of the orange, leaving clearance from the table to reduce the risk of hitting it or rolling the fruit away.
- After gripping, make a small test lift to see whether the orange rises stably with the gripper. If it slips, set it back on the table for support before adjusting the grasp; avoid regrasping while suspended.
- When approaching the bowl opening, keep the orange's lower edge and fingertips above the rim. Release at a position inside with enough room to open, as close to the bottom as practical, to reduce rim contact, tipping the bowl, or the orange bouncing out.

narration: I will use the piper-control skill to start the single real-robot episode with the specified parameters and act on the returned manual and live observations. When finished or unable to continue, I will call finish_episode.

The manual and both views confirm the green orange lies left of the bowl, with only the right arm available. I am adjusting gripper orientation at height, then will reduce step size near the orange and verify the grasp with a test lift.

An orientation adjustment reached a controller joint limit; feedback showed only partial motion. Using the new measured pose, I changed to translating before reorienting. Subsequent moves were normal and the orange has not yet been touched.

The gripper has reached above the orange, and I am checking the fingers' position relative to the fruit from both views. Next I will descend in steps no larger than 1 cm, close once the pads reach its middle, and test-lift.
The orange remains supported by the table, with the fingers on opposite sides and no visible push. I am continuing to descend slightly so the grasp point approaches the wider middle of the fruit.
After a small test lift, the orange has cleared the table with the gripper; neither view shows noticeable slipping. I will raise it above the bowl rim, then move toward the bowl center.
The orange remained in the gripper during transport and is now near the bowl opening. I will align it with the bowl center, lower gradually, release, then check that the bowl supports it stably.

The orange has been lowered into the bowl opening, which has remained stable, with clearance between the fingertips and rim. Next I will lower slightly more, open the gripper, and observe whether it remains stable after release.

After release, the green orange remained in the bowl. It stayed stable after waiting and raising the open gripper; the measured gripper opening was 74.4 mm. The current observation meets the success criteria. I will call finish_episode to close the episode; the on-site operator will confirm the final result.
